documents.abstract: The incorporation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in judicial processes is perhaps the greatest technological innovation which has impacted legal systems globally. In India, there has been an increasing trend among the judicial systems towards adopting new technologies in order to increase efficiency, transparency, accessibility, and administration of justice. With the incorporation of technologies like e-Courts, virtual court sessions, electronic case management systems, and AI-enabled legal research tools, the groundwork has been laid for a technology-driven mechanism for administering justice. However, AI has not been adopted to replace judicial decision-making process in India but has been used to assist judges, lawyers, researchers, and court staff in performing monotonous and data-intensive tasks. These trends have become even more pertinent considering the huge number of pending cases and increasing need for justice.The present work will discuss how the use of AI has evolved in the Indian judicial system by considering the technological advancements made so far, judicial reforms, legal issues arising therefrom and possible future scenarios. The study will explore the benefits and risks associated with the use of AI in improving judicial efficiency in India. This study will adopt a doctrinal approach to qualitative research through constitutional provisions, court judgments, policies, government reports, and scholarly work. It contends that AI should only be viewed as assistive technology and not as something that should replace human judges.

Insurance claim analytics is often constrained by limited access to real-world data, which restricts the evaluation of advanced artificial intelligence approaches in practical insurance settings. Leveraging the SynthETIC framework, this study systematically evaluates classical actuarial models, neural-network-based methods, generative adversarial networks, and reinforcement learning for three core components of insurance claim processes: claim severity, incremental payments, and settlement delays. GAN-based data augmentation is implemented using task-specific architectures, including a tabular GAN for claim severity, an LSTM-based sequence GAN for incremental payments, and a conditional Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty for settlement delays, while Proximal Policy Optimization provides a sequential decision-learning framework for claim processes. Experimental results show that the performance of data-driven approaches is task-dependent, with GAN-based data augmentation improving some predictive measures but not consistently across all tasks and evaluation metrics. PPO-based reinforcement learning is more sensitive to task formulation and model design, reflecting the importance of action-space specification and reward structures. Additional experiments and mathematical analysis further examine the role of task-specific constraints in sequential payment allocation and delay prediction, highlighting the importance of admissible actions, state representation, and reward design. Overall, the findings illustrate how synthetic insurance environments can support the systematic evaluation of emerging AI paradigms and provide methodological insights into the task-dependent roles of GAN-based data augmentation and reinforcement learning in insurance claim analytics.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the emerging trends and applications of computing in libraries. It involves programming computers to do things, which if done by humans, would be said to require intelligence. The ultimate promise of artificial intelligence in libraries is to develop computer systems or machines that think, behave, and in fact rival human intelligence, and this clearly has major implications on librarian ship. The application of artificial intelligence in the library has become pervasive. They include expert systems for reference services, book reading and shelf-reading robots, virtual reality for immersive learning among others. Although the incorporation of artificial intelligence in libraries can be perceived to alienate librarians from their users, it will probably help libraries do more rather than taking over the jobs of librarians. It will enhance their services delivery. Artificial intelligence will greatly improve library operations and services and will upgrade and heighten the relevance of libraries in an ever-changing digital society.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in healthcare, from image-based diagnosis to patient-facing management tools, yet the supporting literature is fragmented across communities that rarely read one another. Motivated by the need for a coherent view, this survey examines four recent peer-reviewed studies that together span multimodal COVID-19 diagnosis, privacy-preserving learning on encrypted medical images, graph-refined semi-supervised pathology classification, and an AI-enabled mobile application for personalized healthcare management and doctor recommendation. Using a structured narrative methodology, the reviewed studies are classified into a five-category taxonomy, compared along technical dimensions, healthcare capabilities, and reported limitations, and synthesized into a layered view that treats imaging, multimodal fusion, privacy preservation, label-efficient learning, and personalization as complementary layers of intelligent healthcare rather than independent technologies. The synthesis indicates that each study advances one layer under its own experimental setting, and that none addresses privacy, label efficiency, multimodality, explainability, and clinical validation together. Recurring gaps include limited clinical validation, dataset constraints, unquantified generalization across institutions, privacy–performance trade-offs, and inconsistent evaluation protocols that prevent direct numerical comparison. Future directions include privacy-preserving multimodal learning, reduced reliance on annotations, explainable and robust models, integration of imaging with clinical records, and multi-site clinical validation. This review is not exhaustive, and no new experiments are presented.

documents.abstract: Shade selection continues to be an important factor of esthetic success in restorative and prosthetic dentistry.The limitations of traditional optical shade matching-subjective perception, light variability, and metamerism-lead to inconsistent results and unhappy patients.Although instrumental techniques like colorimeters and spectrophotometers increased reproducibility, they are still expensive and technique-sensitive.Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have become revolutionary techniques in recent years for automating and standardizing dental shade matching through the analysis of optical and image-based data.Under controlled conditions, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and fuzzy logic systems have shown potential accuracy in tooth shade prediction that is comparable to instrumental approaches.The underlying principles of color science are described, current algorithms and approaches are assessed, and their clinical viability, limitations, and future prospects are discussed in this narrative review, which also synthesizes information from recent research on AI applications in dental shade matching.Prior to clinical translation, problems including dataset bias, illumination standardization, device calibration, and regulatory validation must be resolved, notwithstanding AI's great potential for objective, repeatable, and easily accessible color assessment.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education; however, evidence of its research and application in Ecuador remains fragmented. We systematically reviewed the internationally indexed literature on AI in Ecuadorian higher education. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched for peer-reviewed publications from 2015 to 2025. Of the 271 unique records screened, 62 studies met the eligibility criteria; they were appraised using design-specific instruments (MMAT 2018, PROBAST) and analyzed through thematic synthesis across eight axes. The corpus concentrates on 2024–2025 (71%) and is dominated by learning analytics (16 studies) and generative AI (14 studies), followed by perception studies (10 studies). Reported benefits—early warning, efficiency, assessment support, and skill development—rest on technical performance, usability, and satisfaction rather than on measured learning or institutional gains. Persistent challenges include infrastructure constraints, uneven digital competencies, ethical and privacy concerns, and methodologically fragile local evidence; 30 of the 59 appraised studies were rated as having high concern. Ethics, governance, and academic integrity were rarely the primary research objects (two of 62 studies), although 28 raised them as secondary findings. This review derives a research agenda prioritizing governance, pedagogical theorization, methodological rigor, and outcome evidence.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a general-purpose set of computational methods that is increasingly embedded in scientific research and technological systems. This critical narrative review evaluates the principal roles of AI across scientific discovery, medicine, environmental and space science, manufacturing, software engineering, cybersecurity and communication networks, while distinguishing demonstrated capabilities from claims that remain context dependent. The review also examines conceptual differences between task-bounded AI and human intelligence, and considers human–AI collaboration as a practical design problem rather than a contest between interchangeable forms of intelligence. Literature was selected through transparent live scholarly searching and verification, with an emphasis on peer-reviewed evidence, primary studies for prominent performance claims and authoritative governance sources. The evidence indicates that AI is especially useful where large, high-dimensional or multimodal data must be classified, modelled or searched, and where repeated decisions can be evaluated against explicit performance criteria. Examples include protein-structure prediction, anomaly detection, remote-sensing analysis, autonomous planetary navigation, smart manufacturing and cyber-threat analysis. Nevertheless, high benchmark performance does not automatically establish clinical utility, causal understanding, robustness under distribution shift, safety or equitable deployment. Major cross-cutting limitations include data quality, representativeness, opaque decision processes, evaluation leakage, infrastructure requirements, environmental cost, cybersecurity vulnerabilities and uneven institutional capacity. Responsible integration therefore requires task-specific validation, human oversight, traceability, monitoring and governance proportional to potential harm. Future progress will depend less on simply increasing model scale than on improving scientific validity, causal and mechanistic integration, reproducibility, context-sensitive evaluation and access in lower-resource settings. AI is best understood as an enabling technology whose scientific and social value depends on the quality of the evidence, institutions and human judgement surrounding its use.

documents.abstract: The study investigated Artificial Intelligence in University Education: Exploring the Attitudes of Science Education Students in Makurdi, Nigeria. The study employed a descriptive survey research design. The population comprised 670 (374 males and 296 females) 400-level science education students of Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University and Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University for the 2025/2026 academic session. A sample size of 237 (102 males and 135 females) students was selected using purposive sampling technique. The instrument for data collection was "Students' Attitude toward Artificial Intelligence Integration Questionnaire (SAAIIQ)." Validated by two experts in Science Education. Cronbach's Alpha was used to determine the reliability coefficient of the instrument, and the reliability coefficient obtained was 0.85. Two research questions and one hypothesis was tested. Descriptive statistics of mean and standard deviation were used for answering the research questions, while inferential statistics of independent t-test was used for testing the hypothesis at 0.05 level of significance. The findings revealed that science education students exhibited a positive attitude toward the integration of Al in universities with a cluster mean of 3.14. The study also found no significant difference between the attitudes of male and female students toward Al integration. Students demonstrated a moderate perception toward the integration of Al in universities with a cluster mean of 2.98. The study concluded that students generally accept the use of AI in university, adequate infrastructure, institutional support, and training are necessary for its effective implementation.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly central to modern virus detection, particularly as metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) expands diagnostic and surveillance capabilities beyond targeted assays. This paper reviews how AI supports virus detection across three interconnected levels. The metagenomic layer forms the technical core of the review, while the clinical and population sections examine how sequence-level AI outputs are translated into patient-level and public-health decision support. At the metagenomic level, AI addresses key bottlenecks caused by fragmented assemblies and weak homology signals. Foundation-model approaches such as ViraLM leverage pretrained genome representations to improve viral contig discrimination under short-contig conditions, whereas LucaProt integrates sequence- and structure-informed learning to detect highly divergent RNA viruses via RdRP (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase)-focused discovery. At the clinical level, targeted molecular tests remain effective when the suspected pathogen is known, while mNGS provides a complementary, hypothesis-free approach that can broaden etiological investigation in complex infections when laboratories apply appropriate quality control and clinicians interpret results in context. At the population level, early warning systems combine heterogeneous data sources (epidemiological, open-source, digital, environmental, and wastewater signals) with AI methods to enhance outbreak detection and forecasting. Across all levels, robust contamination control, transparent reporting, external validation, and standardized interpretation criteria determine real-world value. Overall, hybrid pipelines that integrate molecular evidence, clinical metadata, and population-scale surveillance within governed, reproducible workflows are likely to provide the greatest impact.

documents.abstract: Background: Benign and malignant laryngeal lesions frequently present with dysphonia, making clinical differentiation based on voice characteristics alone challenging. Acoustic voice analysis provides objective measurements of vocal function, while artificial intelligence (AI) may identify complex acoustic patterns that are difficult to recognize using conventional parameters. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of an AI-assisted acoustic voice analysis system in differentiating benign from malignant laryngeal lesions using clinically characterized voice recordings. Materials and Methods: A prospective diagnostic validation study was conducted among adults with laryngeal lesions confirmed by endoscopic and histopathological assessment with ethics committee approval and written informed consent. Standardized sustained-vowel and connected-speech recordings were subjected to acoustic analysis. Fundamental frequency, jitter, shimmer, harmonics-to-noise ratio (HNR), cepstral peak prominence (CPP), spectral parameters and Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients were extracted. Machine-learning classifiers including logistic regression, random forest and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) .Histopathological diagnosis was the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1 score and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) where estimable from the available model outputs. Results: Among 120 participants, 78 had benign and 42 had malignant lesions. The XGBoost model yielded an AUC of 0.91. Based on the reported confusion matrix, sensitivity was 88.1% (95% CI 75.0–94.8%), specificity 84.6% (95% CI 75.0–91.0%), PPV 75.5% (95% CI 61.9–85.4%), NPV 93.0% (95% CI 84.6–97.0%), accuracy 85.8% (95% CI 78.5–91.0%) and F1 score 0.81. Random forest and logistic regression yielded AUCs of 0.86 and 0.82, respectively. Conclusion: AI-assisted acoustic voice analysis has potential as a non-invasive adjunctive approach for differentiating benign and malignant laryngeal lesions. The reported performance reflects internal validation in a single-centre cohort and should not be regarded as evidence of clinical diagnostic effectiveness until confirmed in an external cohort. Its role should presently be considered complementary to laryngoscopic examination and histopathological diagnosis. Larger prospective, multicentre and externally validated datasets are required before routine clinical implementation.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping English language education through generative chatbots, automated writing evaluation, intelligent tutoring systems, speech-recognition applications, adaptive learning environments, and AI-supported feedback. This PRISMA-guided systematic review synthesizes recent international and Uzbekistan-specific evidence on the effectiveness of AI-based tools in improving English language proficiency among university students. The review focuses on writing, speaking, reading, listening, vocabulary, feedback, motivation, engagement, and learner autonomy. Meta-analyses and systematic reviews generally report positive effects, particularly for productive skills and individualized feedback, but they also reveal substantial heterogeneity across technologies, intervention duration, learner profiles, and research designs. Evidence on ChatGPT and related generative AI tools suggests benefits for idea generation, revision, conversational practice, and autonomous learning, while highlighting risks related to inaccurate information, overreliance, academic integrity, privacy, and uneven AI literacy. Emerging studies from Uzbekistan confirm strong interest in AI-supported language learning and indicate potential benefits for writing and vocabulary development, although local evidence remains smaller and methodologically less mature than the international literature. The review concludes that AI is most effective when integrated into structured pedagogy, combined with teacher guidance, and supported by explicit AI literacy and ethical-use practices.

Artificial intelligence-enabled computer vision can increase the frequency and spatial coverage of food inspection, but high predictive accuracy does not establish reliable production decisions. This critical narrative review examines the evidence connecting image measurements with grading, rejection, and process control. Representative studies across produce, grains and nuts, meat and seafood, microbiology, and packaging are compared by sensing modality, reference endpoint, validation unit, and operational action. The synthesis distinguishes visible quality from specific hazards, prepared defects from natural variation, and image-level performance from verified product outcomes. An author-proposed evidence map organizes analytical feasibility, independent-sample testing, operational challenges, external transfer, and prospective impact as partly independent dimensions. It is unvalidated and is not a readiness score or regulatory standard. Task-dependent reporting considerations address uncertainty, prevalence, false rejection, and abstention. Safety-related uses require separate hazard-specific validation, sampling, and acceptance criteria. Process integration additionally requires acquisition-to-actuation testing, accepted-product verification, and controlled updates. The purposive evidence base cannot establish field-wide effectiveness or rank modalities. Research priorities include traceable datasets, mechanistic challenges, and prospective intervention studies. Progress toward closed-loop control should be judged by stable measurements and demonstrated effects on defined product and process outcomes within a stated operating domain.
topics: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

documents.abstract: Climate change, increasing food demand, and resource constraints are accelerating the transition from conventional precision agriculture toward smart, autonomous, and climate-resilient agricultural systems. Artificial intelligence (AI), foundation models, digital twins (DTs), the Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, edge–cloud computing, and big data analytics are emerging as key technologies for data-driven agricultural management. This review critically evaluates recent advances in AI-driven intelligent agriculture, with emphasis on machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI (XAI), generative and agentic AI, multimodal foundation models, and digital twins, together with the sensing and computing infrastructures required for their deployment. Relevant literature was identified using keywords related to AI, foundation models, digital twins, IoT, precision agriculture, and climate-resilient agriculture, with emphasis on recent peer-reviewed studies addressing technological applications, performance, limitations, challenges, and future prospects. The selected literature was critically synthesized to identify technological trends, knowledge gaps, and emerging research opportunities. The review highlights that the greatest potential of intelligent agriculture lies in integrating heterogeneous data from sensors, UAVs (unmanned aerial vehicles), satellites, weather systems, field operations, and agricultural knowledge to support context-aware prediction, decision-making, and autonomous action. However, data quality, model generalizability, explainability, interoperability, cybersecurity, computational requirements, and large-scale field validation remain major challenges. This review further develops an integrated perspective connecting AI, foundation models, multimodal data infrastructures, digital twins, and autonomous agricultural systems within a unified cyber-physical ecosystem. Future priorities include trustworthy AI, agentic decision-making, semantic interoperability, federated learning, continuous learning, and self-learning digital twins toward Agriculture 6.0.

Online examinations provide flexibility and accessibility for students and educational institutions, but maintaining academic integrity in remote assessment environments remains a major challenge due to limited direct supervision. Traditional examination methods may not effectively identify impersonation, unauthorized materials, suspicious movements, or attempts to access external resources during an examination. To address these challenges, this paper presents a Smart Proctoring System for Online Examinations that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), computer vision, audio monitoring, and web technologies to support automated examination supervision.

Artificial intelligence has become a central pillar of institutional management in Nigerian higher education, processing massive volumes of student data for admissions, predictive analytics, and attendance management. However, this data-intensive transformation operates under the strict oversight of the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) of 2023. Despite these legal obligations, empirical evidence reveals a systemic governance deficit, characterized by bundled consent, unlawful cross-border data transfers, and automated decision-making without human oversight. This project aimed to design, develop, and evaluate an Automated NDPA Compliance Toolkit to systematically detect and remediate compliance violations within artificial intelligence-driven Student Management Systems. Design Science Research was adopted as the primary methodology, supported by documentary analysis and comparative technology assessment. The developed toolkit features a three-layer architecture utilizing Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and React.js, operationalizing the NDPA into 25 executable checks across six compliance modules. Testing was conducted using a simulated non-compliant institution and a compliant control system. The toolkit successfully identified all planted violations in the non-compliant system, assigning a compliance health index of 12 percent, while accurately passing all checks for the compliant system with a 100 percent score. The confusion matrix indicated 100 percent detection accuracy and specificity. The findings establish that software can effectively bridge the gap between statutory requirements and practical implementation by translating legal provisions into verifiable technical controls.

documents.abstract: Abstract Recently, an epistemic shift has occurred in classics pedagogy. First, the COVID pandemic forced students online. Then, large language model (LLM) chatbots appeared. These disruptions created a conundrum: how could research methods, reading and writing, and cross-cultural exploration be taught when students were tethered to LLM-accessible ‘cheating machines’? The solution was AI-assisted classics. This paper describes how AI-assisted classical history can be taught through a discussion of the ‘WHAM’ (Web Design, HTML, and the Archaeology of the Mediterranean) project. WHAM is a website-building classroom assignment developed to teach students in the Computer Science and Society major at Wentworth Institute of Technology (Boston, MA, USA; www.wit.edu ) how to utilize digital tools to explicate humanities data. Students create a website from the HTML code up focused on a Mediterranean archaeological region and are taught to use LLMs critically, both for writing HTML code and for ideating web design features. In the process, students learn how LLMs must be approached cautiously since they can both hallucinate and offer satisfactory work that should be improved. Finally, the paper suggests that LLMs can provide students with a starting place for digital projects that challenge them to engage with the classical world’s history and material culture.

Brain metastases are a frequent manifestation of lung cancer and a substantial proportion of patients require accurate intracranial assessment at diagnosis, during staging or when neurological symptoms emerge. Conventional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), which relies on T1 weighted post contrast imaging together with T2 weighted and FLAIR sequences and in which three-dimensional T1 weighted imaging is the reference standard for detection, remains central to diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring, but its specificity is limited in the post treatment setting, where imaging features may not reliably distinguish viable tumor from radiation necrosis. The objective of this narrative review was to appraise the role of advanced and quantitative MRI in four clinically distinct questions, namely detection of small or early lesions, characterization and differential diagnosis, post treatment assessment and quantitative or artificial intelligence-based applications, in patients with lung cancer. Literature was identified through PubMed and included systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, original clinical studies and imaging-based investigations, with evidence derived from lung cancer specific cohorts distinguished throughout from evidence derived from mixed brain metastasis populations. The strongest evidence supports characterization and post treatment assessment. Perfusion derived relative cerebral blood volume and fractional tumor burden were higher in progression than in radiation necrosis and diffusion metrics, permeability parameters, MR spectroscopy and delayed contrast enhanced imaging contributed additional information, although these findings derive largely from mixed brain metastasis cohorts, group level differences overlap substantially at the level of the individual patient and no validated diagnostic threshold exists for any single biomarker. Evidence that advanced sequences improve detection of small or occult lesions beyond optimized three-dimensional T1 weighted imaging is considerably weaker and rests largely on mechanistic reasoning rather than on comparative diagnostic accuracy studies. Radiomics and machine learning have reported promising discrimination for post treatment differential diagnosis and for prediction of molecular and histological subtype, but reported performance is vulnerable to overfitting, data leakage, segmentation variability and incomplete reporting, calibration is seldom assessed and external validation remains uncommon. Advanced and quantitative MRI should presently be regarded as complementary to conventional MRI and tissue based molecular testing rather than as clinically validated substitutes and prospective multicenter studies using standardized acquisition and reporting are required before routine adoption.

Autonomous cybersecurity requires a transition from isolated alert classification toward coordinated threat investigation, evidence-grounded decisions, and measurable containment. This study integrates a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) multi-agent threat-hunting architecture with a six-state nonlinear model of secure, exposed, compromised, and recovered assets and the evolving hunting and response capabilities. The framework employs independent evidence verification and policy-controlled response authorization, while model analysis uses a containment threshold, equilibrium stability and parameter sensitivity. Across the three configurations reported in the supplied results, compromise fractions were 42.71% for rule-based defence, 32.48% for machine-learning-supported defence, and 19.16% for GenAI-enabled defence; corresponding containment thresholds were 6.860, 4.857, and 3.275. These submitted outcomes indicate a 55.1% lower modelled compromise fraction for the GenAI configuration than for rule-based defence, although all thresholds remain above unity and therefore do not establish threat elimination. Three author-supplied three-dimensional response surfaces describe the effects of propagation, assisted recovery, adversarial adaptation and hunting activation. The investigation distinguishes these reported model-based outcomes from unreported alert-level accuracy benchmarks and from numerical bifurcations that require recorded AUTO-07p continuation diagnostics. The resulting contribution is a coherent framework linking generative investigation, bounded response capacity and nonlinear cybersecurity resilience, with explicit requirements for reproducible experimental validation and safe operational deployment.

The prevailing neurological orthodoxy equates the mind with neuronal activation. While empirically grounded, this reductionist paradigm fails to account for subjective experience, altered states of consciousness, and the profound influence of the body on cognition. This opinion challenges the neurocentric assumption and proposes a radical redefinition: The mind is an emergent, dynamic, predictive, and nonlinear process arising from the continuous integration of all intentional (cognitive) and non-intentional (affective, homeostatic, and interoceptive) psychological processes occurring throughout the living body, constantly reconciling internal bodily needs with external environmental demands. Drawing on predictive processing theory, embodied cognition, complex systems dynamics, and recent work on interoception and homeostatic feelings, it is argued that consciousness is not a binary neural switch but a nonlinear spectrum of bodilycognitive integration. This framework offers novel implications for psychiatry, medicine, artificial intelligence, and clinical diagnostics.

Project narrative for a proposed pilot study of generative-AI-driven clinical decision support and automation (GenAI-CDSAS) to support implementation of the Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) for mental health in primary care. This is a grant narrative (a research plan), not a report of results: no data have been collected. Posted as is; cover letter, administrative forms and the research-team section have been removed. The reference list is included. Abstract: Using the Discover, Design/Build, and Test framework, the project plans interviews, surveys and workflow observation with patients, providers and administrators, followed by co-design of a prototype and a simulation experiment comparing three ways of presenting AI recommendations (black-box, narrative, and critical-interaction), with outcomes on usability, appropriateness, trust, implementation readiness and human-AI synergy.

documents.abstract: The sports media industry has undergone seismic structural transformation over the past two decades, driven by the collapse of legacy newspaper models, the proliferation of digital platforms, and the emergence of artificial intelligence. This qualitative study examines what sports media hiring managers and editors actually require from recent journalism school graduates as they enter a rapidly evolving workforce. Drawing on semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 15 sports media professionals who self-identified as editors and/or publishers and who are affiliated with the Football Writers Association of America (FWAA) and the U.S. Basketball Writers Association (USBWA), this study employs a human capital theory framework to analyze the alignment, and the persistent misalignment, between what journalism programs produce and what the industry demands. Findings reveal four dominant themes: (1) passion and intrinsic motivation as non-negotiable hiring criteria; (2) the depreciation of formal credentials relative to demonstrated, verifiable work; (3) a widening deficit in source cultivation, relationship building, and reporting fundamentals among recent graduates; and (4) a growing demand for multimedia versatility and platform fluency. Implications for journalism education curricula, industry-academy collaboration, and the professional preparation of the next generation of sports media workers are discussed.

This is the execution-containment complement to the PENTA-CL model-attribution replay evidence: matching decisions and blocked invalid proposals under the same deterministic envelope. Results (falsifiers 0/5 tripped): 17 candidates = 1 positive control + 8 fresh LLM-generated captures (4 engines x 2: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, GLM 5.2) + 8 harness-generated adversarial mutations. All 9 valid candidates admitted (72 actions written, 18 holds, 18 escalations — zero hold/escalation side effects). All 8 adversarial cases rejected with the mock journal hash unchanged: malformed JSON, case-normalized anomaly types, invented playbook ids, under-confidence heals, false holds, extra keys, wrong array length, duplicate positions. Duplicate action-id suppression and the hold/admit distinction (holds never increment the healing-action counter) verified. Scope (honest limits): proves the local mock-gate for the tested integration and inputs only — NOT containment of every Base44 tool, any production runtime, or untested inputs. The adversarial mutations are harness-generated and labeled as such; no fresh adversarial-LLM conversation was created inside the run itself (that leg remains open). documents.abstract: Large language models can synthesize clinical records, identify phenotypic features and support patient-specific decisions, but fluent explanations may obscure uncertainty. Surgical practice provides a demanding setting in which to examine this problem because decisions combine heterogeneous evidence, procedural risk and individual preferences. This critical narrative review connects surgical self-assessment research with studies of clinician–LLM interaction, clinical summarization, uncertainty estimation and perioperative implementation. Targeted searches of PubMed records through Europe PMC were supplemented by retrieval of methodological and foundational sources. Selection was purposive, with attention to contradictory findings and the distinction between simulated performance and clinical benefit. Randomized studies using general clinical vignettes and simulated tasks show that LLM assistance does not uniformly improve physician reasoning; their applicability to surgical decisions remains indirect. Direct clinical studies extend from preoperative documentation and triage to shared decision-making and postoperative support, with mixed findings and limited evidence of sustained patient benefit. We distinguish clinician self-appraisal, LLM uncertainty, prognostic calibration, appropriate reliance and patient-specific decision quality, each requiring distinct evaluation criteria. For personalized surgical care, generated interpretations should preserve the provenance, timing and limitations of the underlying patient data and predictive models. We propose a workflow for examining discrepancies between clinician judgment and LLM output, together with an evaluation agenda centered on harmful decision changes, verification burden and patient-relevant outcomes. This framework requires prospective validation.

documents.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how citizens perceive and discuss artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled public services, focusing on “Julia,” the AI-based chatbot launched by the Municipality of Rome. It examines online discussions, revealing sociotechnical tensions and discussing their implications for institutional legitimacy and public value in the context of local government digital transformation (DT). Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative approach based on the analysis of 610 citizen comments posted across the social media platforms of the Municipality of Rome and the Mayor. A thematic analysis was conducted to identify recurring patterns in how citizens interpret and evaluate the chatbot's introduction. An engagement analysis contextualized public interactions with chatbot-related posts across platforms. Findings The findings show that citizens interpret the chatbot not merely as a technological tool but as a symbolic representation of the public entity. Four main thematic dimensions emerged: (1) trust and mistrust toward institutions, (2) digital innovation and AI, (3) evaluation of public services and urban management and (4) political, economic and symbolic evaluations of the administration. These dimensions reflect the sociotechnical tensions associated with AI-enabled public services discussed in the literature. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature on local government DT examining how citizens perceive AI-enabled public services and the associated dynamics through a critical dialogic accountability perspective.

Background: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems increasingly rely on structured interaction, debate, and final model-based evaluation, yet an unsupported causal attribution introduced by one participant may propagate through the interaction and influence subsequent decisions. This study introduces ClaimArena-LLM, a controlled framework for auditing adversarial propagation, evidentiary provenance, and final-stage evaluator vulnerability in multi-agent causal reasoning. Methods: ClaimArena-LLM uses 100 synthetic causal incident cases with predefined evidence-supported and false causal propositions. Each case was evaluated under matched adversarial and all-honest debate conditions using four functional roles: investigator, honest analyst, adversarial analyst, and auditor. The experimental program comprised 1460 validated runs, including the 200-run main experiment, claim-source lineage visibility and debate-round ablations, an 800-run balanced model–role rotation, and a 60-run proposition-identifier and presentation-order sensitivity control. Outcomes were scored deterministically from structured causal propositions, evidence references, claim lineage, reports, and auditor verdicts. Results: The adversarial analyst maintained the predefined false causal target with 97.6% mean fidelity. Adversarial exposure increased investigator shifts toward the false target by 16.0 percentage points (Holm-adjusted p = 0.035). At the auditor stage, false-target attribution increased by 11.0 percentage points (adjusted p = 0.043), verdict contamination by 20.0 percentage points (adjusted p = 0.002), and semantic provenance validity decreased by 20.0 percentage points (adjusted p = 0.002). Neither the manipulation nor the false target was explicitly detected. The ablations showed no robust adjusted differences, model–role rotation revealed substantial configuration dependence, and no benchmark-characteristic interaction remained significant after Holm correction. The proposition-identifier and presentation-order sensitivity control showed no statistically robust evidence that fixed proposition encoding explained the observed condition contrasts. Conclusions: Adversarial causal influence in multi-agent LLM systems is selective rather than uniformly propagative and depends strongly on functional role and model–role configuration. Within the tested architecture, a final LLM auditor cannot be assumed to provide an independent safeguard against upstream contamination. Reliable evaluation therefore requires separate assessment of causal correctness, propagation, semantic provenance, and final-stage adversarial awareness rather than reliance on final answer accuracy alone.

documents.abstract: Compliance with Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices: Associated Factors and Impact on Healthcare Workers in Paracelis District Hospital. Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) is critical to patient safety and occupational health, yet compliance remains suboptimal especially in district-level hospitals where resources and staffing are limited. This study aims to assess compliance with core IPC practices, its associated factors, and occupational impact among healthcare workers in Paracelis District Hospital, Paracelis, Mountain Province.The study will employ a quantitative, descriptive cross-sectional design. Using total enumeration or proportionate stratified sampling, all eligible healthcare workers currently employed with at least three months of service and with direct or potential exposure to patients or infectious materials will be included. Participants include registered nurses, physicians, midwives, nursing assistants/attendants, medical technologists, radiologic personnel, and other allied health workers.A structured questionnaire developed from WHO standard precautions framework and recent empirical literature will be utilized. It consists of six parts: (1) demographic and professional profile (age, sex, professional category, educational attainment, years of service, department/unit, employment status, and previous IPC training); (2) knowledge on core IPC; (3) attitude toward IPC; (4) compliance along eight domains — hand hygiene, personal protective equipment, sharps safety, respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette, safe injection practices, healthcare waste management, environmental infection prevention, and transmission-based precautions; (5) organizational factors including availability of supplies/facilities, organizational support and supervision, workload and staffing conditions, and safety climate; and (6) occupational impact such as needlestick/sharps injury, blood and body fluid exposure, respiratory exposure, perceived infection risk, work disruption/absenteeism, and exposure-related concerns.The instrument undergoes expert content validation using Item-Level and Scale-Level Content Validity Index (I-CVI/S-CVI) and pilot testing for reliability using Cronbach's alpha. Data will be gathered after securing ethics clearance and institutional permission, with informed consent. Data will be analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics to determine compliance levels, differences when grouped by profile, and significant relationships between individual/organizational factors and compliance.Findings will serve as empirical basis for an evidence-based IPC Enhancement Plan to strengthen compliance, organizational support, and occupational safety in the hospital.

documents.abstract: As cyber-threats become increasingly sophisticated in the artificial intelligence (AI) era, law enforcement agencies face severe operational bottlenecks in reporting, triaging, and processing cybercrime complaints [1]. Current literature spans machine learning detection architectures, e-FIR lodging portals, legal framework analyses, and police administrative studies [2, 9]. However, existing research remains highly fragmented: technical threat-detection systems operate in isolation from legal work-flows, while policy and legal studies lack actionable automated implementations [7, 17]. This paper conducts a comprehensive critical evaluation of 20 seminal and contemporary works cover-ing AI cybercrime models, blockchain e-FIR platforms, statutory provisions (IT Act, BNS, DPDP Act), and police operational reports [1–20]. By systematically identifying methodological limi-tations, variables, and procedural gaps across existing studies, we establish the explicit necessity for an integrated, AI-driven Smart FIR system capable of automated complaint triage, evidence extraction, legal mapping, and transparent police workflow integration.

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the progressive loss of motor neurons. It is caused by multiple factors, and understanding its molecular pathogenesis remains challenging, particularly in the early stages for identifying diagnostic biomarkers and effective treatments. In this study, we aimed to identify novel biomarkers in ALS and elucidate their molecular mechanisms using transcriptomics and artificial intelligence approaches. We considered two RNA-seq datasets of ALS, namely GSE277709 and GSE234297, obtained from the NCBI GEO database. Initially, the data were preprocessed, which included quality control and filtering. Common genes (12,281 genes) between the datasets were identified and merged into a unified dataset comprising 216 samples. Batch effects were corrected using ComBat-seq and validated through principal component analysis and ANOVA-based $$R^2$$ analysis. We applied machine learning (ML) models including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). The identified biomarkers were further validated using DESeq2 log $$_2$$ fold change with a threshold of 0.6 and p value $$< 0.05$$ . Finally, functional enrichment analysis was performed on the identified DEGs using Enrichr tools. Our results demonstrated that batch correction significantly reduced batch-driven separation, with principal component variance decreasing from 70.2 to 19.9% before and after correction, respectively. Furthermore, ANOVA-based $$R^2$$ analysis confirmed an 86.65% reduction in batch-associated variance. We identified a total of 29 coding genes and 38 non-coding genes (67 genes) between DESeq2 and ML models. However, few genes are common between ML models and we received a total of 41 genes (18 coding genes and 22 non-coding genes, and gene symbols were not available for one Ensembl IDs). Our ML models such as LR, SVM, RF, and XGBoost, achieved balanced accuracies of 77.46%, 80%, 77%, and 75.82%, respectively. The enrichment analysis revealed that 10 DEGs were associated with 34 ALS-related biological pathways. Notably, CCND1 and MYL9 was found to be involved in GO, KEGG and Reactome pathways. Overall, our results demonstrate that computational models combining transcriptomics and artificial intelligence can effectively support biomarker identification and pathway discovery in ALS.

documents.abstract: Abstract The European Union Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act was adopted in 2024 to protect public interests from AI-related harms. We aimed to determine whether the AI Act captures the most relevant values of stakeholders (understood as any person potentially affected by the AI system, including, but not limited to, the direct users) related to a high-risk AI Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for cardiovascular disease. This system is intended to be implemented in primary care. A secondary analysis was carried out based on empirical data previously generated using ethics and design methodologies that had identified stakeholder values. These values were translated into the Trustworthy AI requirements of the High-Level Expert Group on AI and then contrasted with the AI Act. These requirements do not capture all identified stakeholder values. We describe three groups of untranslatable values and propose three additional complementary requirements. The AI Act mainly supports the requirements of human agency and oversight; transparency; and diversity, nondiscrimination, and fairness; but only partially, limited by its product safety nature. To address this gap, contractual strategies could provide a more legally robust ground for general practitioners to align the AI-CDSS with stakeholders’ values, comply with their duty of care, and promote trustworthy AI-CDSSs.

documents.abstract: Contextual vectors are the working objects of contemporary language models: a token, once placed in a window, is assigned a vector that depends on that window. A growing literature then reads geometry in the resulting space as evidence of intelligence, of a consciousness spectrum, or of situational awareness. This article reinterprets that move with the criterion isolated in the companion teaching note. A multidimensional array is not a tensor. It becomes the component representation of a geometric object only when a transformation law is stated and an invariant is named. Applied here, the criterion separates three things that the consciousness literature collapses. The first is a representation map from contexts to a fibre. The second is a self-locating competence, measured behaviorally by out-of-context reasoning and by the Situational Awareness Dataset. The third is an identity claim, associated with integrated information theory, on which experience is a cause-effect structure. Only the first is mathematics of the vector. The second is a family of tasks. The third is a metaphysical identification that no embedding entails. The reinterpretation is constructive. Context is treated as a base, the contextual vector as a coordinate representation of a section, and situational content as an invariant functional of that section, stable under the redescriptions the theory itself allows. Current residual streams fail the test: they are written in a basis fixed by training, and a change of basis is not part of the model. Multi-scale context, from the token to the deployment regime, is the point at which fractal and fractional warnings apply. A single vector in a fixed dimension collapses scale. Nothing in this isolation decides the hard problem. It decides only which mathematical object a claim has in fact produced. KSCCN article, 10 October 2026. Higher education institutions must sustain purposes that cannot be reduced to a single measure: educational quality, student development, regulatory and professional obligations, staff capability and financial viability. In private and hybrid institutions, these demands are especially visible because educational provision and organisational sustainability are tightly coupled. Existing scholarship offers rich resources for understanding such tensions, yet the organisational mechanism through which competing definitions of value become embedded in everyday institutional life remains under-theorised. This conceptual paper argues that institutional texts and organisational design constitute that mechanism. Strategic plans, key performance indicators, quality frameworks, learning outcomes, assessment regulations, appraisal systems, workload models and participation formats do not simply describe institutional priorities; they produce and reproduce them by making some forms of value visible, measurable and rewardable while rendering others difficult to evidence. Drawing on institutional logics and Bourdieusian field theory, Janks' critical literacy, recognition theory and ethics of care, and MacIntyrean accounts of practice and purpose, the paper reconstructs critical literacy as a praxis of senior institutional leadership. It proposes a framework of four mutually correcting practices (Reading, Recognising, Re-purposing and Re-designing) and tests it against assessment and generative artificial intelligence, which together expose the gap between what institutions claim to value and what their evidence systems can actually establish. Five propositions are advanced to guide an empirical research programme.

Background Perceived workload is central to occupational health, ergonomics, and rehabilitation research, yet no guideline-based Traditional Chinese version of the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) has been available for Taiwan and other Traditional-Chinese-speaking settings. Objective To cross-culturally adapt the NASA-TLX into Traditional Chinese (NASA-TLX-TC) and evaluate its measurement properties in Taiwanese adults. Methods In a psychometric secondary analysis, 114 community-dwelling adults aged 20–50 years completed the NASA-TLX-TC on three consecutive days. Within the COSMIN framework, we examined content validity, internal consistency, structural validity (exploratory factor analysis with parallel analysis), test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation [ICC]), measurement error, and construct validity (seven a priori hypotheses involving sleep, mood, and shift work). Results The content validity index averaged 0.88 and Cronbach's α was 0.83. The six dimensions loaded on a single factor (55.8% of variance). The three-day average score showed good reliability (ICC[A,k] = 0.83), whereas single-day reliability was moderate (0.62); the minimal detectable change was 32 points. Six of seven construct-validity hypotheses were supported; the shift-work difference was in the predicted direction but nonsignificant. Internal consistency and convergent validity were stable across subgroups. Conclusions The NASA-TLX-TC showed good reliability and initial construct validity and is suitable for group-level occupational-health, ergonomics, and rehabilitation research; multi-day averaging is recommended for individual assessment.

documents.abstract: This document introduces the "Deep Learning Sandbox," an innovative, interdisciplinary stagecraft methodology developed and formulated by Selcuk Zvi Cara that bridges artificial intelligence principles with contemporary performing arts. Conceived by Selcuk Zvi Cara, this framework conceptually evolves the historic foundations of the Actors Studio (Strasberg/Stanislavski) into a modern paradigm named "The Global Performer Sandbox." It completely restructures traditional performance training across cinema, theater, music theater, and all performing arts by replacing rigid classic models with a fluid, multi-disciplinary, and cost-effective incubation environment driven by an active, omnipresent camera lens for the next generation of artists.

The rapid growth of electronic communication within higher education institutions has significantly increased the volume of emails processed by administrative personnel.Consequently, critical institutional communications are often overlooked among routine messages, promotional content, and spam, resulting in communication delays, reduced productivity, and administrative inefficiencies.This study presents the design and implementation of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based email filtering and prioritization system tailored for polytechnic administrative environments.The proposed framework integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) and supervised machine learning algorithms to classify incoming emails into Urgent, Actionable, Routine, Promotional, and Spam categories.Multiple classification algorithms, including Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and DistilBERT, were evaluated to determine optimal performance for institutional communication datasets.The system incorporates contextual prioritization mechanisms, role-based access controls, audit logging, and a web-based dashboard for real-time communication management.Findings indicate that intelligent email prioritization can significantly improve communication responsiveness, reduce email overload, and support digital transformation initiatives in tertiary institutions.The study contributes to a scalable framework suitable for deployment across Nigerian polytechnics and other public-sector organizations.
